facts.text: 0.95-Meter Schmidt Photometer was deployed at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit during Kepler Space Telescope in 2009.
facts.source: NASA Ames Research Center / Ball Aerospace

facts.text: 0.95-meter aperture Schmidt telescope with a 1.4-meter primary mirror focusing light onto a curved focal plane array of 42 CCDs totaling 95 megapixels.
facts.source: NASA Ames Research Center / Ball Aerospace

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Measured the ultra-tiny dip in starlight (down to 10 parts per million) caused by an exoplanet transiting in front of its host star.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit.
The most prolific planet-finding instrument ever constructed in human history.

scenes.kids: I am 0.95-Meter Schmidt Photometer. I arrived here at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit in 2009.
scenes.explorer: 0.95-Meter Schmidt Photometer, Kepler Space Telescope: deployed at Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit in 2009.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.
